verses.1: On that day, Moses’ list was read to the people. It was written there that my people will not come before God in the future. They will never be able to do so ever again.
verses.2: For the children of Israel did not endure suffering and death before they could be redeemed. They were subjected to oppression and cruelty by those who wanted to curse them. Our God was turned into a source of curses instead of blessings.
verses.3: And when they heard the Torah, they separated every city in Israel from one another.
verses.4: And before this, the priest Eliezer placed it in the ark of our God, near to the place where the good things are kept.
verses.5: And he made a large tent for him. Inside that tent, the offerings of bread and other foods were placed there. There were also the offerings related to the laws of the Levites, as well as those related to the priests and the scribes.
verses.6: And in all this, I was not in Jerusalem. In the year thirty-two, during the reign of King Artaxerxes, I went to see the king. For several days, I asked him various questions.
verses.7: And I went to Jerusalem. And my father did something bad: he made Eliezer a priest, so that he could be an officer in the court of the Temple.
verses.8: And great suffering befell me; I was forced to abandon all the utensils of the house of Tobiah, which were taken from the temple.
verses.9: And she said, “Let the vessels be cleaned, and let all that belongs to the house of God be returned there. Let the offerings and sacrifices be placed back in their proper places.”
verses.10: And I knew that the sheep were not given back to their owners. So, they ran away to graze on the fields. The sheep and the workers who did the work of farming…
verses.11: And she attacked the scribes, and said, “Why did you leave the house of God? I will catch them and make them stand in their places.”
verses.12: And all of Judah brought their livestock, their flocks, and their herds, as offerings to the gods.
verses.13: And he appointed as leaders over the possessions of Shemaiah, the priest, and Zadok, the scribe. He also appointed Pedaiah from the tribe of Levi. They were considered trustworthy, and they received a share among their brothers.
verses.14: May Your God remember this, and may You not forsake the kindness I have shown in Your house and in Your temple.
verses.15: In those days, I saw in Judah people who were carrying goods on their shoulders. They brought goods like grapes, figs, and all kinds of other items. They brought them to Jerusalem on the day of Shabbat. I will testify about this on the day of Mikra.
verses.16: And the merchants will sit there, bringing all kinds of goods. They will sell their products during Shabbat to the children of Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.17: And she complained about the wicked deeds of the Jews. She said to them, “What kind of evil do you do? You desecrate the Day of Retribution.”
verses.18: Behold, this is what your ancestors did. Our God has brought upon us all this evil. He has brought this disaster upon this city. And yet, you continue to slander Israel, trying to destroy it.
verses.19: And when the gates of Jerusalem were opened on the day of Passover, they said, “Let the doors be closed until after Passover.” And from my youth, I stood at the gates, so that no one could enter on the day of Passover.
verses.20: And the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods from outside Jerusalem came once or twice.
verses.21: And I will testify against them, and I will say to them, “Do you really want to stand against the Lord? If you change your minds, then I will send an army against you from that time onward. But they did not come back at that time.”
verses.22: And she said to the Levites, “Be pure and come to guard the gates on the day of Shabbat. This is also a reminder from my God, and a sign of His great kindness towards me.”
verses.23: Also in those days, I saw that the Jews brought back their women who had been captured as slaves.
verses.24: And among them, half speak Aramaic, and they do not know Hebrew. They are not able to understand Jewish language at all.
verses.25: And I will curse them and despise them. I will speak evil of them before God. If they give their daughters to their sons, and if they take their sons’ daughters as wives for their sons, then so be it.
verses.26: May those sins of Solomon, king of Israel, never be repeated in the many nations. He loved his God greatly, and God made him king over all of Israel. But he also led those women astray, causing them to commit immoral acts.
verses.27: And may you not do all this great evil to our God, so as to bring back the foreign women into His service.
verses.28: And from the descendants of Yoaydah, son of Elyashiv, the high priest, there was a bridegroom named Sanbalat. And they married him.
verses.29: God reminded them of the priests and their covenant with God.
verses.30: And they will be purified from all impurities. They will stand among the priests and Levites, each doing his own duty.
verses.31: And for the sake of those trees that are planted in times of need, and for the sake of those branches that remind me of my God’s goodness.
